neighbours.label: Public exposure gained by something: coverage, publicity, attention, visibility, media success; vs the same nouns in non-media senses (insurance coverage, paying attention, experimental success)
fire: After the scandal broke, the senator's office drew intense coverage from cable news.
Organizers hoped the celebrity guest would bring the festival some free publicity.
Her viral video earned the small bakery national attention almost overnight.
The award gave the young author much wider visibility among literary critics.
Analysts said the stunt was a public relations success for the airline.
The lawsuit generated unwanted publicity for the toy company last winter.
Thanks to the documentary, the remote village received worldwide media attention.
The band's surprise rooftop show got huge press coverage in every newspaper.
quiet: After the storm passed, the homeowner's policy offered limited coverage for roof repairs.
Organizers hoped the warm weather would bring the festival some extra visitors.
Her careful baking earned the small shop loyal customers over several years.
The new lenses gave the young astronomer much sharper images of distant galaxies.
Engineers said the bridge repair was a technical success for the city.
The recall caused unexpected costs for the toy company last winter.
Thanks to the new well, the remote village received clean water for the first time.
The band's long rehearsal improved their timing on every song.

predictions: Fire 0.5-1.0 on publicity/coverage/attention nouns in media contexts; near misses with the same words in other senses under 0.1.
notes: Card: ' publicity' x7, marketing, media, coverage.
